evidence.text: Money on the Street( German: Geld auf der Straße) is a 1930 Austrian- German romantic comedy film directed by Georg Jacoby and starring Lydia Pollman, Georg Alexander and Franz Schafheitlin.

evidence.title: Money on the Street

evidence.title: She-Devils on Wheels
evidence.text: She-Devils on Wheels is a 1968 American exploitation film about an all-female motorcycle gang called The Man-Eaters, directed and produced by Herschell Gordon Lewis.

evidence.title: Edward Yates
evidence.text: Edward J. Yates( September 16, 1918 – June 2, 2006) was an American television director who was the director of the ABC television program" American Bandstand" from 1952 until 1969.

evidence.title: Rumbi Katedza

evidence.title: Herschell Gordon Lewis
evidence.text: Herschell Gordon Lewis( June 15, 1926 – September 26, 2016) was an American filmmaker, best known for creating the" splatter" subgenre of horror films.

evidence.title: Herschell Gordon Lewis
evidence.text: He is often called the" Godfather of Gore"( a title also given to Lucio Fulci), though his film career included works in a range of exploitation film genres including juvenile delinquent films, nudie-cuties, two children's films and at least one rural comedy.

evidence.title: Herschell Gordon Lewis
evidence.text: On Lewis' career, All Movie wrote," With his better- known gore films, Herschell Gordon Lewis was a pioneer, going farther than anyone else dared, probing the depths of disgust and discomfort onscreen with more bad taste and imagination than anyone of his era."

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: Devils on the Doorstep( literally" the devils are here") is a 2000 Chinese black comedy film directed, co-written and produced by Jiang Wen, starring Jiang himself, Kagawa Teruyuki, Yuan Ding and Jiang Hongbo.

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: Shot in black and white to mimic old- time war movies, the film premiered at the 2000 Cannes Film Festival on 12 May and clinched the Grand Prix.

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: The film was initially not allowed to be shown in theaters in China for a certain period but was eventually made commercially available in China since.

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: Inspired by the novel" Survival" by You Fengwei," Devils on the Doorstep" is set in the last years of the Second Sino- Japanese War during World War II and tells the story of a Chinese villager who is forced by a mysterious figure to take custody of two prisoners from the Japanese Army( Teruyuki and Yuan).

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: Fearing both the mystery man and the Japanese, the village falls into a dilemma over what to do with the two prisoners.

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: Contrary to its title," Devils on the Doorstep" is not at its core an anti-Japanese war film.

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: In Jiang's own words, the film shows how Chinese literature and film has perpetuated an attitude of blaming the aggressor and casting the Chinese population as passive victims of aggression.

evidence.title: Devils on the Doorstep
evidence.text: Jiang hopes that the film illuminates this common human psychological trait of blaming others for disaster that goes beyond Chineseness.
